q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a carbonated soft drink per litre?
title: Soft drink carbon footprint per litre
short: Add the sugar, concentrate, CO2 gas and treated water per litre, then the bottle or can, cap and label. Add the plant's water treatment, syrup room, filling and chilling energy divided by litres filled. Packaging is often the largest share.
audience: Soft drink bottlers and contract fillers

ul: Sugar, concentrate and treated water per litre.
Carbonation CO2 bought, counted at its supplier figure.
PET bottle, glass bottle or can, cap, label and shrink film.
Blow moulding, if you make PET bottles from preforms.
Filling, chilling, compressed air and bottle washing for returnable glass.

p: Report per litre by pack size, since a small bottle carries more packaging per litre than a large one.

example.title: Worked example: bottling line per litre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 162,500 / 2,000,000 = 0.0813 kg CO2 per litre
Add sugar, concentrate, CO2 and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
